source.title: Tyr Progression: configurable three-mode XP economy, unified MXP default, additive source awards and cross-Path reward calibration
source.body:
## Owner-locked architecture (2026-11-21)

**Implement support for ALL THREE modes**, configurable server-side and preferably per Path where practical, with **one shared currency / MXP-only as the shipped TMM default and current target**. This is an implementation requirement, not a request to implement only one of the alternatives.

1. **`unified` — DEFAULT:** one persistent universal XP/point wallet, currently internal `tyr_progression:mxp`, buys *all* Core and Path purchasable traits (combat, physical, magic, etc.). Path activities as well as qualifying magic expenditures can award MXP. No independent spendable Monk/Hunter/Dragon/other-path points in this mode. Path milestones/deeds and rank prerequisites still gate paid/unlocked abilities; any mastery display must not secretly create a second spendable XP wallet. Specify how existing native 20-level automatic abilities/milestone gates work without requiring a hidden second XP system.
2. **`hybrid`:** shared MXP wallet buys all skills; separate Path-specific mastery XP/levels track non-spendable proficiency, granting licenses/auto abilities/level prerequisites. Path and magical activities may both award MXP when eligible, *without* silently converting Path mastery XP one-for-one.
3. **`separate`:** independent Path XP, rank and spendable Path points purchase local skills; global MXP still buys universal Core. Distinct independently qualifying activities may affect both. No cross-ledger conversion or shared global-state wipe on Path change.

**Configuration contract:**
- Server-default mode `unified`; configurable global or explicit Path-level override; permit skill-level `currency`, `level_system`, earned-source routing, amounts, multipliers, quotas, bonus eligibility, milestone/level prerequisites and optional native points when mode permits.
- Preserve independent third-party native Dragon Survival/JAWR advancement where still provider-owned; adapt to the common model instead of assuming upstream systems can be reconfigured just by JSON.
- Newbie centrally earns zero shared MXP. Normie gains global MXP from ordinary existing magic sources and Core skills. Specialist Path-specific sources only activate on valid active enrollment. Retain one-path MXP modifier per actual award and leave Path ranks dormant out of Path; shared Core and wallet persist (#455).
- All Path types should be representable (Monk, Hunter, Dragon species, Gilded, Bare Zerker, Dryad, Sexy Demon, Sapient Slime, Spawn and other existing planned paths), not a Monk-only hardcoded implementation. Avoid changing user-facing term "MXP" without separate decision.

## Crucial owner correction: additive independent accomplishments

**One gameplay action can award the SAME shared currency more than once where it satisfies independently defined reward sources.** Never suppress a legitimate second source just because an event/transaction has already earned another source's XP.

**Canonical example:** Iron's Spellbooks' **Spectral Hammer**:
- Qualifying successful mana expenditure: award the appropriate **magic-use MXP**, normalized from nominal mana cost versus starting pool, once per committed resource transaction.
- Each *successfully broken qualifying block* from that cast: separately award **block-break MXP** according to the active Path/source rules, one verified reward per actual qualifying block; TreeChop/AoE instrumentation should not compress 20 valid blocks into one.
- These are additive. E.g. first-level illustrative 40% of starting mana bar = **400 base MXP**, plus 12 eligible blocks at proposed 10 each = **120**, **520 total base MXP** before the appropriate lifetime-level growth divisor (which may change while processing a large award).
- Distinguish **two legitimate source categories** from **duplicate callbacks** for a single source. Dedup keys must include (player, source category, committed operation and, for physical block awards, verified block position/target or equivalent unique ID). Do not use a global action-only dedup key that accidentally consumes the later independent category.
- Canceled/protected/unsuccessful breaks, failure to spend a genuine resource, fake-player automation and duplicate callbacks never receive XP. A no-cost successful spell may earn block-break MXP but not magical cost MXP. Preserve global first-boss/ritual award rules and per-Path source caps.
- All rewards still hit the **one** shared `mxp` wallet in unified mode; no automatic generic "XP for any block" given to unspecialized Normie unless a registered source expressly says so.

## Calibration anchor — owner-locked standard

- **One complete first-accessible personal magic resource pool equals one first-level point**, i.e. **1,000 base MXP** for the full nominal pool. Current `MxpMath.GOAL=1000`, `normalizedBase(nominalCost,firstAccessiblePool)=1000×ratio`, `growth_factor=1.02` on live `dev/progression`. Keep normalized nominal cost before efficiency; require successful actual debit for resource credit.
- Nonmagic activity rewards are defined in **the same base-MXP unit**, by expected effort/danger and verified completion. These are *not* required to have identical per-action awards.
- The old Monk native `experience_systems/monk.json` points (**pickaxe block 1; log 2; hostile kill 8 + unarmed 4; food discovery 10; advancement 25; petting 2**) and Hunter native `maxHP/4` are on unrelated legacy/native curves and **must not be carried forward unchanged** into unified 1,000-MXP-per-point spending.

### PROPOSED starting numbers — owner review, not finalized implementation balance

| Eligible, source-verified accomplishment | Proposed base MXP | First point equivalence |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Monk qualifying ordinary barehand block (stone, etc.) | 10 | 100 blocks |
| Monk qualifying barehand log break | 15 | ~67 logs |
| Approved hostile kill (20-max-HP mob) as a Path activity | 40 (2 per max HP, with filters) | 25 kills |
| Monk *additional* unarmed hostile kill bonus | +20 (1 per max HP) | combined ~17 unarmed kills |
| Hunter specialty bonus on approved prey | 2× normal Hunter kill activity XP | ~13 specialty kills at 20 HP |
| First completed consumption of a distinct qualifying food | 100 | 10 food discoveries |
| Valid one-time ordinary advancement | 100 | 10 distinct advancements |
| Monk legitimate animal petting | 10 with cooldown / anti-spam | 100 interactions |
| Player-paid magical use | 1000 × nominal resource / first resource pool | one full starting pool |

Food discoveries and advancement awards are **finite** (per player/ID) and need independent balancing so they do not swamp routine activities. Hostile kills must avoid artificial max-HP buffs, fake repeated death/respawn and bosses' special payouts. These are **comparative calibration candidates only**, to be validated against mana regeneration throughput, block-breaking speed with/without TreeChop, combat pace, and real early-game progression, NOT owner-approved exact final values. For paths lacking settled earning actions, retain configurable placeholders and avoid invented unconditional XP streams. Avoid simple reversible placing/breaking block farms.

### Source findings (dev/progression; source audit only)

- `XpChannel.MXP` is reserved and globally persistent; `MxpMath.GOAL=1000`, server default growth 1.02. `Wallet.magic` awards a global point per 1000 effective XP.
- `ChannelConfig` already supports per-tree/per-skill XP channel, purchase currency and `level_system`, but `ChannelConfig.bind` **disallows direct milestone XP/points into magic wallet**, `ProgressionApi.recordFiltered` **skips** magic channels for ordinary activity sources and `ChannelEngine.grant` explicitly rejects magic XP. `ChannelEngine.magic` uses transaction-level dedup and growth. Need a **new verified ordinary activity-to-MXP settlement path** (with per-source independent dedup), plus coherent level/milestone gating in `unified`.
- `dev/progression` `monk.json` has 30 skills (29 automatic + one paid), rank XP thresholds through Monk 20. `hunter.json` has 31 skills and own XP/point economy. Legacy PR #379 has three MXP-purchased Monk pilot skills; reconcile rather than copy stale `tmm_progression` IDs.
- `ProgressionEvents.blockDrops` records generic block and barehand block under confirmed drops event; modded AoE and spectral spells may not identify a `ServerPlayer` as breaker. Need source-verified attribution adapter, but not an invented event that claims every client-side block deletion.
- `core.json` is currently MXP channel with zero skills (pilot PR #379 has Core additions). Do not assume pilot is merged.
- No default full-build/Prism authorization. No code modification claimed by this issue.

## Ready work slices
1. [ ] Add a versioned server-controlled economy policy/schema with `unified`, `hybrid`, `separate`, safe reload/state tests and explicit per-skill wallet/level-system routing.
2. [ ] Implement source-category-aware unified MXP grants using existing `MxpMath` growth/point math. Per-source dedup rather than whole-action suppression, cancellation safety, source IDs and cross-provider provenance.
3. [ ] Migrate/select Path earning event definitions for unified mode; no duplicate Monk native point accrual in unified; establish meaningful Path milestone/automatic ability gates and ensure retained Core MXP.
4. [ ] Audit and implement verified Iron's Spectral Hammer and other spell-AoE actual block-break attribution. Allow XP from mana debit **plus each verified block break**. Do not pay per drop/packet.
5. [ ] Benchmark equivalent effort against 1 full baseline bar; calibrate Monk first and report proposed values plus time-to-first-point on path, then Hunter, Dragons, other Path sources. Keep nonapproved numeric proposals separated from locked mechanics.
6. [ ] Unit tests for all 3 policy modes, startup/reload, purchase/refund/Path changes, one wallet in unified, two ledger gates in hybrid, independent wallets in separate, per-Path config, additive dual-source same action, dedup of same callback, Newbie veto, high-level divisor transitions.
7. [ ] After quick CI and owner-authorized build only, test Minecraft client/server including Spectral Hammer, TreeChop, ordinary hand break, Botania repair, pet kills/XP, Dragon native progression and real source-provider XP.

**Engineering:** shared Tyr Progression `compat/progression` code through isolated `feature/progression-*` PR targeting `dev/progression`, not a standalone Path runtime; coordinate active issue #455, Monk #271/#59, scope #390 and branch policy. Separate actual code and QA from design approvals.

## Tentative tree budget and backward XP calibration — owner (2026-11-21)
**Status: TENTATIVE owner planning target, not a finalized numeric cap or new runtime behavior.** The owner proposes **no more than 500 total spendable skill points invested to max out a single tree**. A player may have access to **three trees**, making an illustrative **1,500-point** lifetime spend to max them all. Do not interpret as 500 nodes, 500 points per branch, an XP earning cap, a prohibition on all-path mastery, or every tree necessarily costing 500. Free automatic abilities and milestone unlocks do not consume this budget. Total tree purchase costs = sum of all skill rank prices including prerequisites and capstones; this is the unit to budget.

**Back-calculation from locked starting unit:** 1 point per **1,000 effective MXP**, equivalently full first-accessible personal magic pool when fully expended (subject to correcting baseline capacity for the pinned starter book). At 1,500 points, total effective MXP earned = **1,500,000**, excluding other special points from direct awards or refunds. But routine *base* MXP is divided by `growth^P` where `P` counts earned lifetime MXP points; therefore total raw ordinary XP for `N` points, from zero, is `1000 * (growth^N - 1) / (growth - 1)` (or `1000*N` for growth=1). This follows source `MxpMath` per-level recomputation and assumes no fixed un-divided boss/first-ritual awards.

| Growth | Raw XP to 500 pts | Raw XP to 1,500 pts | Raw XP for final 1,500th point |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 500,000 | 1,500,000 | 1,000 |
| 1.001 | 648,309 | 3,478,331 | 4,474 |
| **1.002 (assistant candidate; unapproved)** | **857,784** | **9,512,725** | **19,985** |
| 1.003 | 1,157,212 | 29,470,922 | 89,145 |
| 1.005 | 2,221,368 | 354,713,591 | 1,765,739 |
| **1.020 (current)** | **997,778,457** | **~397,399,802,751,094,656** | **~7,792,152,995,120,508** |

**Design implication:** Current `growth_factor=1.02` is unusably steep for ~1,500 lifetime paid points, independently of how generously individual Path activities are rewarded. Recommend seriously testing 1.001–1.003 (1.002 is a starting proposal only), or a different soft/saturating growth curve; leave it server-configurable. The fixed/ordinary reward exceptions must remain accounted for. Don't silently change `MxpMath.DEFAULT_GROWTH` without a reviewed code/config change and owner-approved numerical target.

**Next balancing method:** (1) inventory total rank prices for Core and every proposed Path tree and draft budgets <=500 per tree, preserving expensive all-branch maxing; (2) compute required ordinary *raw* XP at 100, 250, 500, 1,000 and 1,500 lifetime points for chosen curves; (3) compare real time-to-point in early/mid/late gameplay by mana expenditure, barehand mining, spell mining (separate additive magic+blocks), ordinary/specialty kills, rituals, pets, discovery; (4) tune source awards and growth factor together, rather than choosing 100-block vs 20-block first-point conversion in isolation; (5) verify respec spend/refund does not reset lifetime `P`, milestone requirements or grant additional points, and skill purchases cannot exceed tree budget; (6) validate players who own three compatible trees can spend their accumulated one currency without clobbering each other's Path ranks.


## Sustainable automation throughput stress test — Mahou and Neo Vitae (2026-11-21)
**Balance research, NOT an owner-approved change to the growth factor.** Source/docs from the actual mod authors and current repository historic adapters indicate that **sustained personalized resource expenditure**, especially maintained boundaries and Neo Vitae networks, may dwarf manual casting and make a 1.02 growth divisor reachable late-game if these are eligible MXP. Before replacing default growth=1.02 with 1.002/1.005/1.01, stress-test the actual full 300-point trajectory **against highly optimized automation**, not just manual bars or hand breaks.

### Numeric target
At 1,000 effective XP/point and ordinary growth 1.02, **100, 200 and 300 total points** from zero require about **312,232; 2,574,245; 18,961,725 cumulative BASE XP** (no fixed awards). Current first-accessible source denominator is fixed; boosting max pool/regen increases **sustainable expenditure per second** but doesn't change base MXP per unit expenditure.

### Mahou Tsukai Boundary of Drain Life
Author wiki https://mahoutsukai.stepsword.com/spells/drain-life-boundary/ states **default 5 Mahou spent per active circle per ONE SECOND** (`DRAIN_LIFE_BARRIER_MANA_CYCLE=1` in *seconds*, not ticks); active Drain Life circle limit **10** per player https://mahoutsukai.stepsword.com/guides/casting-and-scrolls/. Under continuous payment **10 circles = 50 Mahou/s**. XP first-accessible Mahou baseline B is **TBD** in TMM's source registry; examples, not verified pack values:
- `base XP/sec = 1000*50/B` if ALL those paid maintenances are eligible and credited to an online owner.
- B=100 → **500 XP/s**, **~10.4 minutes to 100 points**, **~1.43 hours to 200**, **~10.53 hours to 300**. B=200 doubles times; B=500 yields 100 XP/s, ~52.67h to 300.
- Extremely fast first 100 points compared with late remaining 100. Costs may be drawn from **Mana Circuits instead of personal mana**, with source-specific funding/ownership questions. The mod *regenerates mana from successful Drain Life target activity*. A circle may continue to pay when monsters are absent, but whether there is a valid paid/owner source callback for idle cycles must be verified. Current TMM Mahou MXP adapter is a future P1 target, not demonstrated active gameplay. **Never treat farm energy production as XP, only qualifying successful debits.**

### Neo Vitae Serenade feeding four Thermalilies
- First accessible Neo Vitae **Novicius Anima orb B=5,000 EV** is a committed original denominator. If qualifying owner-attributed running EV network debits are allowed, `base XP/sec=0.2*(EV actually spent per second)`. Example rates: 100 EV/s gives **20 MXP/s** and ~**263h** to 300pts; 500 EV/s gives **100 MXP/s** and ~**52.7h**; 1,000 EV/s gives **200 MXP/s** and ~**26.3h**. These rates are **scenarios, not verified Serenade costs**.
- Neo Vitae ritual stats are data-map configurable (`activation_cost`, `refresh_cost`, `refresh_time`, `per_operation`); actual effective pinned Serenade entry remains to be inspected. Its actual **EV debit rate** cannot be inferred merely from the number of Thermalilies consuming lava. Check if ritual pays continuously, pays per successful placement, backs off when tank/placement blocked, or remains running while no lava can be used.
- Four Thermalilies produce **Botania mana**, but **generation alone is not MXP** under the established portable-funded Botania debit contract. If that mana is subsequently spent by a qualifying player-operated item, it may earn distinct Botania MXP, subject to actual debit and source conditions. Beware of manufacturing a cross-system generation→infinite spend→MXP feedback loop.
- Existing archived Neo Vitae `AnimaEvent.PostSyphon` adapter precedent: any owner-bound **actual EV-network expense including automated upkeep was eligible while owner online**, pending balance revisit. In current integrated code, verify exactly which active hooks inherited this policy; not a promise every unattended effect qualifies.

### Decision to surface
**Passive upkeep eligibility is a balance gate, not merely a numerical curve problem.** Owner chose additive independent accomplishment awards (spell cost + verified block breaks). Do NOT conflate this with automatically paying all machine maintenance. Ask/record whether owner-controlled ongoing circles and rituals are intended to earn MXP while actively maintained, while player online, while machine/owner is offline or chunkloaded, and whether personal vs circuit/network-paid costs count. Distinct source categories may add XP; duplicate processing of the *same debit* must never multiply XP. Anti-overflow fractional batching and no server tick loops per individual XP grant may be required at high rates.

**QA stress test**: sample authoritative source telemetry [owner, source ID, real cost, nominal cost, baseline pool, validated operation, active/online, observed XP/sec, lifetime P] on fresh build at 1, 4 and 10 Mahou circles, plus Serenade with 0, 1, 4 Thermalilies and different lava consumption states; compute true time-to-100/200/300 vs expected. Check effective owner and funding source, no inactive/paused or no-cost payouts. Don't change canonical growth factor or XP source eligibility without owner decision.


## Owner-revised complete-tree purchase budgets — Monk 1,000; most Paths 100 (2026-11-21)
**This supersedes the earlier tentative <=500-point per-tree and generic 100-point Monk target in this issue and prior conversation.** The owner now wants:
- **Most Paths:** *target* roughly **100 total purchased points** to buy every rank/node in that complete tree. Treat as a design budget, not an engine-enforced XP/skill ceiling; tree-by-tree balance can vary.
- **Monk:** *target* **1,000 total purchased skill points** for complete five-branch mastery (Martial Body, Conditioning, Footwork, Hands as Tools, Magical Cultivation) **in addition to its free automatic base techniques**. ~200-point/branch average is illustrative, not a forced equal allocation; the costs should provide greater granularity.
- Keep one universal `tyr_progression:mxp` currency by default for all purchased traits across all Paths, with `unified`, `hybrid`, `separate` configurable alternatives as previously locked; purchases from Core/other accessible trees advance the same *lifetime MXP level/divisor*.
- The user's stated starting Mahou capacity is **100**. A new Mahou user cannot sustain one Drain Life circle, much less ten; maximum continuous operation is a late-game investment. It is invalid to project the maximum ten-circle farm rate back to a new player's starting earning rate.

### Full mastery burden — IMPORTANT EXPONENTIAL MATH
Using native `MxpMath.GOAL=1000` effective MXP/point, `growth^P` divisor on ordinary base awards, and zero initial levels:
```
raw base MXP needed for N ordinary-earned points = 1000 * (g^N - 1) / (g-1)
```
The existing TMM **growth factor 1.02** implies **~19,913,232,532,907 raw MXP for 1,000 Monk points** (~19.9 trillion, not million). If earning 500 base MXP/s continuously from ten successful 5 Mahou/s drain circles with baseline 100, that's ~1,263 real-life years. This is mathematically incompatible with a usable 1,000-point tree under any remotely ordinary playthrough, even before the extra Core/Path purchases. **Do not treat previous ~19M/300-point projections as relevant to the new Monk target.**

| Growth g | Raw to 100 pts | Raw to 1,000 pts | Raw to 1,100 pts (Monk + Core 100) | Raw to 1,200 pts (Monk + Core + Path 100) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1.000 | 100,000 | 1,000,000 | 1,100,000 | 1,200,000 |
| 1.002 | 110,579 | 3,187,156 | 4,002,603 | 4,998,394 |
| 1.003 | 116,418 | 6,331,845 | 8,659,676 | 11,800,510 |
| **1.005 (candidate, unapproved)** | **129,334** | **29,115,125** | **48,072,293** | **79,288,464** |
| 1.010 | 170,481 | 2,095,815,564 | 5,668,961,402 | 15,333,655,681 |
| 1.020 (current) | 312,232 | 19,913,232,532,907 | 144,264,323,083,612 | 1,045,143,968,542,223 |

**Candidate curves 1.002–1.006, a capped 1.02 divisor or similar saturating growth model remain open pending throughput measurement**. No owner approval to change the live growth factor yet. At 1.005, the last of 1,000 levels requires ~145,846 raw XP (vs first 1,000), and cumulative rewards to Monk milestones: level100 ~129k, 300 ~693k, 500 ~2.22M, 700 ~6.37M, 1000 ~29.12M.

### First-pass Monk XP opportunity audit and what is/is not live
Existing `dev/progression` `experience_systems/monk.json` grants native Monk XP: barehand logs (2), pickaxe-tag blocks (1), qualifying hostile kills (8), additional unarmed kills (4), food discovery (10), advancements (25), animal petting (2); see `ProgressionEvents` and `TreeChopXpBridge` for completed-drop and per-felled-log attribution. These original native amounts are **wrong units for 1,000-MXP-per-point default** and must be replaced/calibrated, not copied.
- Candidate ordinary Monk training 30–50 **base MXP/legitimate block** makes the first point ~20–33 blocks before other sources. Benchmark speed and farming rather than setting irreversible per-block values today.
- Qualified player Ars Touch→Break (~15 nominal mana, first-accessible MXP denominator still configured as 100) gives **~150 base MXP from magic expenditure + each independently qualifying destroyed block's configured MXP**. A novice book has ~150 maximum mana and ~6 mana/s replenishment before other upgrades; at hypothetically 40 MXP per block, that's ~190 base XP per successful cast, with a regenerative ceiling of 24 casts/min **if actually continuously cast against valid blocks**. This is **~274k raw XP/h theoretical uptime upper scenario**, not a realistic early-world measured rate. Validate actual pinned XP denominator / Novice book capacity conflict with "one full starting bar = one point".
- Shared awards also include successful mana use by Iron's, player-held Botania repair, Neo Vitae EV, Psi, properly eligible Mahou, boss/ritual/discovery milestones; **do not presume all hooks live**. In `dev/progression` `MxpService` handles magic resource and boss receipts, with legacy/source audit of adapters. Verify current hooks and player attribution against exact build.
- Mahou Drain Life default documented operation: 5 Mahou/s per sustained circle; 10-circles at B=100 **500 base XP/s** only at endgame and **only if paid upkeep counts / player owner is eligible**; circles do not self-sustain at initiation.
- Neo Vitae Novicius starting orb B=5,000 EV, so actual credited EV/s yields 0.2 base XP/EV spent, but Serenade of the Nether's real refresh cost/timing needs native exact-version audit; four Thermalilies do **not** imply a fixed EV/s rate. Botania produced mana is no MXP until independently eligible item expenditure. 
- Additive source rule persists: one Spectral Hammer use grants **mana MXP + independently verified qualifying blocks MXP**, with dedup per source, not per entire cast.
- Fixed first-time boss/ritual awards bypass routine divisor; include these finite once-only contributions in later calculations but don't let them masquerade as sustainable income. Respec and spending do not reset lifetime P.

### Next decision-quality measurement
1. [ ] Generate **Monk purchase ledger** for five branches to total ~1,000 invested points, keeping currently free 30 native abilities free.
2. [ ] Source-audit/measure **active early**: no equipment/newbie→Monk initiation, hand block mining, TreeChop logs, one hostile kill, 15-mana Touch→Break; realistic verified rewards/minute including travel, resource regen and discovery.
3. [ ] **Mid**: advanced spell mining, AoE, natural MXP regeneration and portable mana, Neo Vitae personal EV, advanced martial throughput.
4. [ ] **Late**: actual legal optimal burst/sustain from Ars, Mahou circles, Neo Vitae Serenade, Botania mana spends, relevant Path XP bonuses, 1/4/10-circle scaling; require verified resource debits, no duplicate callbacks and no offline free XP without explicitly approved rule.
5. [ ] Model **phased progression time** against cumulative 1,000 + any simultaneous Core/other Path points; simulate multiple `g` curves and compare with gameplay target. The 1.005 candidate requires 29.1M base XP for 1,000; at 100k base XP/h constant ~291h, at 500k/h ~58h, and at 1.8M/h ~16.2h. These are hypothetical steady rates, **not real elapsed playtime**, as power must be earned.
6. [ ] Code/schema support three XP modes in shared Tyr Progression only; TMM defaults unified; don't change hardcoded default economy curves or source values until reviewed. Source-level CI, then only explicitly owner-authorized in-game build/QA.


## Proposed Monk Magical Cultivation skill: Enlightenment (owner idea, 2026-11-21)
**Status: owner-proposed concept under discussion, not locked for implementation or released.** Skill **Enlightenment** has 18 purchasable levels, each intended to **reduce the per-lifetime-level ordinary MXP exponential growth factor by 0.001** for *future* awards. If the default growth starts at `g_base=1.020`, the intended factor is `g_effective = max(1.000, 1.020 - 0.001 * enlightenment_rank)`. At 18/18, g=1.002. Preserve config support for alternative base growth factors, tier magnitude/rank counts and per-player modifiers; **do not grant paid ranks with zero benefit** when configured base growth falls below 1.018. This is a Monk fifth-branch (**Magical Cultivation**) candidate, not an automatic global default reduction for all Paths.

**Critical semantics:** In the planned **unified currency mode**, Enlightenment improves the **global ordinary MXP award calculation while the player owns and can actively benefit from the Monk ability**, regardless of whether the validated independent award source is mana spending, block breaking, killing or other eligible actions. It does not multiply nominal resource costs, bypass activity eligibility, credit unearned blocks, change first-boss fixed XP policy, or grant separate Path XP in default unified mode. It does not recalculate/reward historical awards, retroactively mint points or reset the immutable lifetime MXP level `P`. For out-of-Path/dormant skill and combined-Path policies, resolve through existing eligibility and deterministic modifier resolution. Do not stack two independent growth-reducer skills without an explicit configured aggregation rule.

**Economics from exact current `MxpMath` effective XP formula** (`1000*g^P` ordinary base XP per point at lifetime P):
- `g=1.020` throughout: ~19.913 **trillion** total raw XP to 1,000 points; point #1000 alone ~398.3 **billion**.
- `g=1.011` throughout (9 ranks active from start, hypothetical): ~5.126 **billion** total to 1,000; 1,000th point costs ~55.8 **million**.
- `g=1.002` throughout (18 ranks from start, theoretical lower bound): ~3.187 **million** total to 1,000; point #1000 ~7,359 raw XP.
- If player has no Enlightenment until cumulative lifetime P=100 and instantly gets all 18 then (upper approximation rather than real ramp), total to P=1,000 ~**3.389 million** raw XP. If delayed until P=300, ~**21.74 million**. If progressively gained over the first 100 lifetime points, linear 18-rank adoption gives ~**3.23 million** base XP total. Thus **unlock pacing matters greatly**; granting most ranks only deep into the 1,000-point tree causes an artificial progression wall before the remedy can be purchased.

**Design decisions to settle before implementation:**
1. Whether all 18 ranks should be accessible no later than roughly lifetime level 100–150, with increasing costs/prerequisites, versus another explicit unlocking curve; permanent cost should count against the Monk's full-tree ~1,000-point budget.
2. Per-rank purchase cost, 5th-branch prerequisites, and whether a skill that is nearly mandatory to reach 1,000 should be a transparent early development spine rather than a late-tree capstone.
3. Configurable base/growth and meaningful rank cap. If base <=1.018, 18×0.001 would reach clamp 1.000 before final rank; disallow zero-effect purchases or parameterize the rank stride from base minus desired minimum.
4. Test the **actual cumulative cost with ranks bought throughout a playthrough**, not incorrectly assuming 18/18 always on from P=0; compare simultaneous Core/other Path purchases and real earning rates.
5. In `hybrid` / `separate` modes, specify whether Enlightenment reduces only the global MXP growth and does not alter native mastery/Path-specific XP curves unless configured.

**Engineering feasibility / readiness:** `MxpMath.apply(..., growth)` already takes variable `growth`, and `ProgressionApi.awardMagic` currently supplies only `MxpProgressionConfig.GROWTH_FACTOR.get()`. A shared per-player resolved growth modifier could be injected through `PathRegistry` skill eligibility, with clamp and server-authoritative persistence. It must be applied by EVERY unified MXP award handler and not fork the engine into separate Monk math; src/unit and runtime testing required. No implementation/CI/QA implied.


## Owner decision: Enlightenment immediately purchasable; no-drop stone credit and hardness scaling (2026-11-21)
**Decision locked:** `Enlightenment` (18 ranks at 0.001 growth reduction each, configurable and no retroactive payout) is the **very first purchasable Monk skill accessible upon successful Monk initiation**, without a secondary progression-tree prerequisite or tier-2 gate. First rank should have a low initial **MXP** price and count toward Monk's ~1,000 purchased-point budget; subsequent ranks can use progressively increasing prices, but all are reachable early enough to meaningfully affect the player's progression curve. The first rank is accessible, not auto-granted for free; shared global MXP currency applies in unified mode. Individual rank costs are to be designed, not assumed here.

**Source-audited early stone mining bug, not runtime PASS:** On `dev/progression`, `ProgressionEvents.breakBlock` deliberately does **not** award XP on pre-commit `BlockEvent.BreakEvent`, whereas `ProgressionEvents.blockDrops` calls `ProgressionApi.record(...barehandBlockBreak...)` only from `BlockDropsEvent`, after verifying empty event tool and empty main hand. NeoForge **1.21.1** docs https://github.com/neoforged/Documentation/blob/main/versioned_docs/version-1.21.1/blocks/index.md#breaking-a-block state **`Block#playerDestroy` / `Block#dropResources` / `BlockDropsEvent` occur only if `IBlockExtension#canHarvestBlock` returns true**. Consequently, an ordinary fist break of stone before native hand harvest tier unlocks (current `hand_harvest` auto at Monk rank 4) can destroy the block yet yield **zero Monk XP and zero progress toward `trial_five_stone`**. The issue is the missing *event*, not merely an empty `getDrops()` list. Do not falsely claim it currently works. **Required fix:** award for independently verified, successful player-caused post-commit barehand block removal regardless of whether it drops items or passes harvestability; no XP for a canceled/protected/failed block-break attempt. Preserve successful TreeChop per-removed-log credit and precise spell attribution. Strongly prefer a single authoritative completed-break event/transaction with original pre-removal blockstate and empty-hand information; a pre-event alone is unsafe, and a drop-event alone omits no-drop breaks.

**Hardness scaling is design proposal, not yet owner-locked:** Standardize a per-block XP function based on the source `BlockState.getDestroySpeed(level,pos)` *hardness*, **NOT** current player's effective mining speed. Proposed baseline 35 base MXP for 1.5-hardness stone; `xp = round(35 * clamp(sqrt(max(0,h)/1.5),0.5,4.0))` for eligible nonzero-hardness natural/legitimate training blocks. Approx dirt h=0.5 → 20; stone h=1.5 → 35; oak log h=2 → 40; deepslate h=3 → 49; obsidian h=50 → 140. This scales with effort without rewarding a 50-hardness block ~33× more than stone, which is highly farmable after advanced mining upgrades. Proposed global per-source tuning parameters: base, reference hardness, minimum/maximum multiplier, category overrides, player-placed/replaced block handling and anti-repeat. Never reward negative-hardness/unbreakable blocks or infinite instant-break junk by default. Do not assume hardness is time-to-break after personal buffs; benchmarking should record effective post-skill blocks/minute and XP/minute at multiple Monk ranks, including hard ores and stones.

**Required QA:** Fist-break ordinary stone before hand-harvest unlock **without drops** grants completed-break Monk XP and advances `trial_five_stone`; with hand-harvest unlock/drop still only one payout; fist logs, dirt, deepslate, obsidian, unbreakable block, broken/protected/cancelled events, repeated place/break and TreeChop credit tested; spell-break awards nominal mana + separate physical block results where eligible; rank-1 Enlightenment is purchasable immediately after first-sunset initiation using shared MXP and affects only future ordinary awards. Verify no duplicate award if both break and drop callbacks fire. Do not report tested or implemented by posting this goal.


## Player-placed obsidian farming: balance consequence (2026-11-21)
**Player raised a challenge to anti-farming limits; no new owner-locked prohibition.** Using **175 BASE MXP per legitimate obsidian block** (hypothetical; previously proposed hardness cap was 140), at lifetime P=100 and five successive ordinary MXP points:
```
number_of_blocks = ceil(sum(1000 * effectiveGrowth^P for P=100..104) / 175)
g=1.020 (0 Enlightenment): 216 blocks
g=1.011 (9/18 Enlightenment): 88 blocks
g=1.002 (18/18 Enlightenment): 36 blocks
```
At full Enlightenment `g=1.002`, a five-point interval starting at P=500 is ~78 blocks, P=900 ~174 blocks, and P=995 ~210 blocks; total ordinary base XP to earn first 1,000 P (assuming full Enlightenment from P=0, theoretical lower bound) ~3.19M = ~18,213 qualifying 175-XP obsidian breaks. These numbers show a repeated place/break cycle can be an effective grinder once mining is instantaneous and Silk Touch returns obsidian; this is **not automatically an exploit** in a magic-heavy automation pack.

**Recommended default review direction:** Do not add blanket 'no XP for player-placed blocks' or arbitrary diminishing returns just to prevent intentional training/farming. Recognize actual successful, player-attributed removal (regardless of item drops), require eligible Path/source and anti-duplicate callback/transaction protection; no payout for canceled/imaginary removals or fake-player automation unless separately configured. Natural vs player-placed filtering, placement cooldown or cap may be an optional config only if later measured in-game balance justifies it. The number to tune initially may be the hardness reward (~140–175 for obsidian), the Enlightenment point-cost/unlock curve, or activity throughput instead of suppressing legitimate mining.

**Decision remains OPEN:** whether deliberate repeatable placed-block training is permitted by default. Do not implement a restrictive anti-farm rule without confirming the owner's intended gameplay.


## Hardness reward direction approved: linear and universal block eligibility (2026-11-21)
**Supersedes** prior proposal for capped square-root hardness scaling and default player-placed mining anti-farming. **Owner-selected design direction:** Monk XP for **all legitimately broken block types**, including modded blocks, without authoring a per-block whitelist; base reward scales **linearly with original block hardness** and is credited regardless of harvest drops. Blocks can be player-placed/replaced/rebroken for XP without special anti-farming restrictions. Correctness protections stay: server-verified completed removal, real attributable actor, no fake/canceled/protected breaks, no duplicate awards for the same block, and preserved additive spell mana **plus** independently broken blocks. Scope is eligible Monk training means (fists and properly attributed qualifying spell mining), not granting Monk XP for any arbitrary machine mining automatically.

**Illustrative owner-supplied high-hardness example**: 1,750 base MXP for obsidian at hardness 50, equivalent to a candidate linear coefficient **35 base MXP per hardness point**. Not yet an owner-locked numerical coefficient; if used it yields stone hardness1.5→52.5 base MXP, log hardness2→70, deepslate hardness3→105, obsidian hardness50→1750. Fractional awards must be accumulated precisely/deterministically, not rounded to zero via integer-only native event APIs. Nonbreakable hardness below zero (bedrock etc.) never qualifies as a completed survival break; zero-hardness blocks may earn a **tiny configurable minimum** if legitimate, with no per-type whitelist. Use `BlockState.getDestroySpeed(level,pos)` on original pre-removal state, without scaling by current player's effective speed/mining perks or loot outcome. Do not impose a hidden upper cap on high-hardness modded blocks without evidence.

**Vanilla mining counterexample:** Per https://minecraft.wiki/w/Obsidian ordinary empty fist obsidian requires ~250s (50 hardness), and per https://minecraft.wiki/w/Breaking stone takes ~7.5s (1.5 hardness) without a proper tool. At coefficient 35/hardness, both earn **7 base MXP/s** at unmodified fist speed. Hence literal vanilla-hardness scaling is naturally time-calibrated rather than an obsidian exploit; enhanced Monk native harvest and mining speed can progressively raise XP/s as intended.

**Full Monk 1,000-point example:** With full Enlightenment effective divisor g=1.002 *from the very beginning* (theoretical lower bound), first 1,000 lifetime points demand ~3,187,156 raw ordinary MXP; at 1,750/block that is **1,822 obsidian blocks**, ~**126.5 h** continuously at 250s/block, not ~15h at 30s/block. Real early ranks have higher growth until Enlightenment is bought; later equipped skill/harvest improvements dramatically change speed and should be benchmarked independently. At original g1.02 the same calculation is intractable, reinforcing early Enlightenment as first purchasable skill.

**Implementation follow-up:** Migrate post-commit physical block credit off harvest-gated `BlockDropsEvent` to a reliable verified removal path with original blockstate/hardness and player identity, so no-drop barehand stone advances Monk XP and milestones; preserve all-block TreeChop and AoE attribution and distinct parent mana-expense credit, avoid per-block whitelist filters, migrate default unified award arithmetic to accept fractional/large amounts. Tests should cover non-dropping stone, player-placed obsidian, hard mod blocks, 0-hardness blocks, unbreakables, Silk and drop vs no-drop, plus per-block money arithmetic. Neither code nor gameplay QA is claimed complete.


## Current implementation handoff: Monk 1000-point draft + Enlightenment first vertical slice (2026-11-21)
- [Draft PR #478](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/478) **complete design ledger**: machine-readable 37 unique purchased skills, five lanes exactly **200+200+150+150+300 = 1,000 MXP points**, includes 20-point baseline Focus and the first-purchase 18-point Enlightenment, preserving 29 free native skills. All numerical ability outputs beyond approved Enlightenment and live Focus are provisional until the optimized endgame gear benchmark. No runtime JSON altered by this design PR.
- [Draft engine PR #479](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/479) **generic per-player growth reduction implementation**: `xp_growth_reduction` handler validation, clamp via pure `GrowthFactorMath`, player-eligible purchased-effect sum in `ExperienceGrowth`, central `ProgressionApi.awardMagic` integration, four JUnit test methods. Applies only to future ordinary MXP, without retroactive XP or fixed first-time reward changes; engine branch `feature/progression-enlightenment-growth-modifier-2026-11-21` -> `dev/progression`.
- [Stacked draft Monk PR #480](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/480) **first live-path purchasable Enlightenment skill**, 18×1 shared MXP point, available immediately at Monk rank 1 after initiation, effect 0.001/rank. Config branch `feature/monk-enlightenment-first-purchase-2026-11-21` -> engine branch, to be retargeted to `dev/progression` after #479 merge. Live Monk definition becomes 31 nodes (29 free automatic, 2 paid including Focus); #478 remains full authored design, not 37 runtime-active nodes.
- **Source validation:** PR #478 generator assertions verified node count, price sums and prerequisites; GitHub CI reported bootstrap/pinned boss/standalone Progression/JAWR module jobs SUCCESS on blueprint commit `850a4c2`. Engine/config CI were still in-progress at initial check; do NOT assert module/build PASS until results arrive.
- **Still blocked by #475:** unified MXP *default* earning/purchasing across all Paths, independently additive magic+hardness block awards, no-drop stone fix #59, three configurable currency modes. Do not treat this initial Enlightenment vertical slice as implementing these policies. Explicit owner authorization still required for integrated server/Prism smoke and gameplay acceptance.


## Monk purchased-trait source reconciliation ready for next QA — 2026-11-22
**Owner explicitly requests next-run Monk trait gameplay tests.** A complete no-duplicate crosswalk is documented in [PR #481](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/481), `compat/progression/design/tree-drafts/MONK-PAID-TRAIT-CROSSWALK-NEXT-QA-2026-11-22.md`. It reconciles **all 37** proposed paid skills to 30 currently active native Monk abilities, 18 historically implemented retired Tyz specializations, existing generic Progression handler types and the newest owner XP/tree decisions.

**Actual new runtime source:** 29 purchased traits added **as JSON only**, no gameplay Java changes; previous 29 automatic abilities remain free, Focus is preserved, new first-purchase Enlightenment included. Coherent source (including stacked #479 growth engine and #480 Enlightenment config) currently defines **60 Monk nodes: 29 automatic and 31 purchased**, covering **868 of 1,000** intended paid MXP points. **Six 132-point skill proposals are held** because of true source-semantic gaps: Piercing Palm (armor bypass), Fortunate Hands (Fortune/Silk exclusivity), Stone Resonance (hardness-gated speed), Overworld Bounty (ore loot), Spellward (cross-provider magic ward semantics), and Meditative Elixir (potion-duration adapter). Historical native Monk XP amplifier and extra native point grant were deliberately not resurrected under the planned unified MXP model. Generic data adapter source is reused rather than reimplemented; there is no second Tyz engine.

**Review-ready dependency sequence:** [engine #479](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/479) -> [Enlightenment config #480](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/480) -> [trait config #481](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/481). Frozen final candidate `5b92bb6d21e6dab5f1606c13c58af33960aa8c64`. All four relevant source CI/Gradle workflows **PASS** at that exact commit. The earlier 12 test failures were resolved by expanding 15 canonical magic-stat aliases into the same native attributes consumed by strict source tests; no tests disabled.

**Next-test intake:** [PR #482](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/482) registers mandatory next owner-authorized comprehensive unstable integration inclusion attempt in `docs/qa/LIVE-TEST-INCLUSION-REGISTER.md`, exact source frozen, A/B game acceptance, known holds. The integration writer must merge/reconcile the stacked sources and register inclusion without blindly overwriting the shared pack; no integration assembly, Prism package, server/client gameplay validation or publication has been run by this source-only work. Next-gameplay acceptance must not claim default three XP economy modes or hardness/no-drop block awards from #475/#59 are fixed; they remain separate engine tasks.


## Owner revision 2026-11-22: typed ward split, remove redundant mining perks, universal beneficial duration
**Approved design supersedes earlier 37-node proposal and six-unimplemented-traits hold list.** The tree is now **38 purchased Monk skills / 1,000 total points**, split Martial Body 200, Conditioning 200, Footwork 150, Hands as Tools 110, Magical Cultivation 340, while retaining all 29 free automatic Monk powers.
- **Deleted (not renamed or deferred):** Stone Resonance (hardness-gated mining speed) and Overworld Bounty (extra ore drops). Existing Barehand Efficiency, Fortune and loot progression cover the niche without redundant skills.
- **Four independent defensive skills use only exact vanilla incoming damage-type IDs**, *not* magical origin/caster/mod classification or broad fire tags: Spellward `minecraft:magic` (16 ranks, 16% max), Alchemical Ward `minecraft:indirect_magic` (10 ranks, 10%), Withering Ward `minecraft:wither` (5 ranks, 5%), Dragonbreath Ward `minecraft:dragon_breath` (5 ranks, 5%). All reuse generic `damage_multiplier` by `damage_tag` and remain unarmored. Fire and explosion are separately covered by existing Elemental Tempering via `#minecraft:is_fire`/`#minecraft:is_explosion`. Do not count modded caster fireballs as Spellward magic if the applied DamageType is fire.
- **Meditative Elixir:** 10 ranks, +2%/rank, extends *all* newly received finite `MobEffectCategory.BENEFICIAL` durations on the player regardless of origin (consumed/splash potions, spells, ritual, beacon). Uses generic `beneficial_duration_bonus` in existing `OwnedEffectDurationMixin` (not a potion-source inventory scan). Harmful/neutral/infinite statuses unaffected; hidden chained instances skipped; preserve original effect amplifier and refresh semantics.
- **Fortunate Hands:** built-in Fortune connector was already present. New optional `mode_key`/`mode_value` guard in the existing virtual Fortune calculator enforces native Treasure Hand's *Fortune OR Silk* mutually-exclusive mode, at most +3 virtual Fortune.
- **Piercing Palm:** reuses generic conditional `attribute` for `apothic_attributes:armor_shred`, provisional 1%/rank to 20%, pending pinned loaded player attribute and damage QA.
- **Review-ready owner PRs:** generic Progression engine [#485](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/485) on `dev/progression`; Monk config [#486](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/486) stacked on earlier #481 -> #480 -> #479; full budget/design [#478](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/478). CI-only combined proof [closed #487](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/487) source commit `117fd8cfc715e4c2eebd8baa9dbf83f634787136`: all **four** GitHub module workflows passed, including strict JSON read. #487 must **not** be merged as a second source copy.
- **Next-run inclusion request updated** [#482](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/482): test the 67 loaded Monk abilities (29 free, 38 paid) and specific damage types, Fortune/Silk, potion duration from all sources, respec, relog, and source-specific 85% performance. This is source CI **not** owner gameplay/Prism QA; integration writer must reconcile owning PRs before a frozen test build.
- **Still separate:** #475 default unified/hybrid/separate MXP currency and linear hardness award; #59 credited post-commit stone without drops; no claim those are fixed by these two PRs.


## Advancement-point pricing correction and possible Quest Shop exchange (2026-11-22)
**Owner-locked universal skill purchase rule:** one purchased rank costs exactly **one advancement point**. All non-Monk Paths target **100 advancement points / 100 purchasable ranks** for a single fully mastered build, even when the total visible alternatives of mutually exclusive choices exceed 100 (Hunter: 62 common + one 8-point Training Style + one 30-point Favored Prey = 100). Monk remains **1,000 points / 1,000 ranks**. No `base_cost>1`, escalating `step_cost`, or `rank_costs>1` in the final approved scheme. Historical source ranks must be migrated with equivalent capped benefits and old-save purchase receipts validated. Design-only new docs: [#495](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/495) and [#478](https://github.com/heatwaveqc/Too-Much-Magic-Modpack/pull/478). The current playtest Monk source #486 and older live Hunter **have not** been repriced yet.

**Feasibility proposal — selling skill points for Quest Shop coins (NOT YET OWNER-APPROVED):** Existing Quest Shop `/hqs shop` has a **team-shared coin balance** and FTB Quests supports one-time per-player command rewards, but the shipped `/tyrprogress admin xp` awards *native Path XP*, not the MXP wallet. Don't sell native points or bypass the central earned-MXP ledger directly. Add a small trusted server-side redeem operation (permissioned command or bound voucher redeem) that calls central MXP settlement with **fixed +1000 effective MXP** per redeemed purchased point. Via `MxpMath.fixed` this grants exactly one lifetime MXP level and one spendable point while retaining fractional progress, increments lifetime P for future routine-award divisor, and cannot be amplified by source grinding/Enlightenment; obey Newbie/creative/spectator eligibility. Use unique server-generated receipt/transaction ID and one redemption per paid item to prevent replays. Redeem/deduct coins atomically if using a direct shop action; if the existing team coin shop cannot guarantee atomic credit on command failure, sell a consumable player-redeemable voucher and consume only after successful server grant. Ensure **team-owned currency** cannot silently broadcast personal XP points to every member (avoid `team_reward:true`), handle refunds/relog/respec safely, and use late-game pricing/maximum purchasable point budget only after owner balance decision. A one-time fixed +1000 MXP is *not* 1000 ordinary base MXP and cannot be implemented via `awardMagicOrdinary`, which is growth-divided. If multiple vouchers are redeemed each should be a separate legitimate fixed reward transaction.
